memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "God also said to Moses, "I am the Lord. I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob as God Almighty, but by my name the Lord I did not make myself fully known to them."" - Exodus 6:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before God says anything about what He will do, He says who He is. I am the Lord.

That order matters. God does not comfort Moses first with promises about the future. He steadies him first with His own identity. Our confidence is meant to rest on God's character, not on our circumstances improving.

Then something remarkable is said. The patriarchs knew God as God Almighty — the One with power to protect and provide. But they did not know Him in the full covenant-keeping reality that His name the Lord carries. That deeper knowledge was about to be revealed through an act of redemption.

God reveals Himself progressively. Each generation was given more, until finally He revealed Himself completely in His Son. Hebrews puts it beautifully: in the past God spoke through the prophets, but in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son (Heb 1:1-2).

We stand where Abraham never stood. We know the God of the burning bush by the face of Jesus Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I find my stability in God's character or in my circumstances?
2. How well do I actually know the God I say I believe in?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are who You are, whatever my situation. Help me to know You more deeply through Jesus Christ. Amen.
